qAndA.question: What is the technique used to capture high-resolution images of Jupiter from Earth?
What is the weight of a 100lb person on Jupiter?

qAndA.answer: Gaps in the cloud cover, not due to cloud color variation.
qAndA.question: What are the dark spots in Jupiter's Great Red Spot?
What is Jupiter called in Hawaiian?

qAndA.answer: Because Io has many volcanoes, and Pele is the Hawaiian goddess of volcanoes.
qAndA.question: Why might the goddess Pele want to rest on Io sometimes?

text_to_speech: welcome to jupiter my name is jamika from the international gemini observatory a program of nsf's nora lab jupiter is the fifth planet from the sun it's about five times as far as the earth so a year on jupiter it's about 12 years on earth jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system so about 11 times the radius of earth if you weighed 100 pounds on earth you'd weigh 252 pounds on jupiter now jupiter has 53 named moons and another 26 awaiting official names for a combined total of 79 moons fun fact researchers using a technique known as lucky imaging with the gemini north telescope have collected some of the highest resolution images ever obtained from the ground as part of a multi-year joint observing program with the hubble space telescope in support of nasa's juno mission the gemini images when combined with the hubble and juno observations reveal that lightning strikes and some of the largest storm systems that create them are formed in and around large convective cells over deep clouds of water ice and liquid the new observations also confirm that dark spots in the famous great red spot are actually gaps in the cloud cover and not due to cloud color variation enjoy the rest of your trip through the solar system on to saturn

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: My name is Jumeca from the International Gemini Observatory, a program of NSF's Nour
Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun.
It's about five times as far as the Earth, so a year on Jupiter is about 12 years on Earth.
Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system, so about 11 times the radius of Earth.
If you weighed 100 pounds on Earth, you'd weighed 252 pounds on Jupiter.
Jupiter has 53 named moons and another 26 awaiting official names for a combined total of 79 moons.
Fun fact, researchers using a technique known as Lucky Imaging with the Gemini North Telescope
have collected some of the highest resolution images ever obtained from the ground
as part of a multi-year joint observing program with the Hubble Space Telescope in support of NASA's Juno mission.
The Gemini images, when combined with the Hubble and Juno observations,
reveal that lightning strikes and some of the largest storm systems that create them
are formed in and around large convective cells over deep clouds of water ice and liquid.
The new observations also confirm that dark spots in the famous Great Red Spot are actually gaps in
the cloud cover and not due to cloud color variation.
Enjoy the rest of your trip through the solar system onto Saturn.

Next up is Jupiter!

Join Jameeka Marshall from NSF's NOIRLab, International Gemini Observatory as she talks about the biggest planet in our solar system. Afterwards, join Matt Brown from the W.M. Keck Observatory as he talks about the Asteroid Belt in ʻōlelo Hawai'i!
